properties.decision: Which node survives a merge is a person's choice. The engine proposes and a person picks: propose_heal ranks both candidates and gives the reason for each (provenance, connections, status, priority, which is newer), recommends one only when a real difference separates them, and never deletes on a tiebreak; apply_heal keeps the survivor the person chose.
properties.name: Which node survives a merge is a person's choice: the engine proposes, a person picks
properties.rationale:
THE OWNER'S WORD. Anthony, 2026-10-13, on the judgement pass, recorded on chg:the-owner-rules-on-items-17-to-25-of-the-judgement-pass-2026-10-13. His words: "Go with your recommendations." Item 23 ("Fix the merge-survivor rule ... consult status, priority and connectedness, or leave the survivor to a person") is recorded there as accepted and carried out when done, in these words: "merge survivor: the engine proposes and a person picks, after a root-cause pass". The plan he approved said: if the rule itself is the cause, supersede it with "the engine proposes, a person picks".

THE ROOT-CAUSE PASS FOUND THE RULE ITSELF IS THE CAUSE (fact:root-cause-a-merge-deletes-the-wrong-node-because-the-survivor-rule-is-blind-to-status-priority-and-connections-2026-10-14). heal.rs did exactly what dec:merge-survivor-provenance said, provenance and then the node id, and read nothing of status, priority or connections. On 0.83.5 the id decided all 11 same-type pairs in this design; ctr:anthony (10 edges) was kept over who:ajs (1,353), and a medium, accepted requirement over a critical, proposed one; and apply_heal refused the swapped operation a person would have used to correct it.

WHAT IT REPLACES. dec:merge-survivor-provenance (BL-29, 2026-07-20: provenance, id breaks ties) and dec:a-tied-merge-breaks-by-degree-not-by-alphabet (a degree tiebreak whose accepted status was never the owner's word, fact:the-degree-tiebreak-decision-read-accepted-without-the-owners-word-2026-10-14). A degree tiebreak still deletes on a tiebreak, and keeps the wrong node in the 09-29 rename case; a person picking would have stopped all four known cases. It also ends the history of decision:ack:d0098626ac85ac53, the 2026-09-15 ruling that kept the id tiebreak "UNCHANGED, DELIBERATELY" and answered the finding with disclosure ("the alphabet chose the victim"): the alphabet no longer chooses, so that disclosure is gone.

HOW IT MEETS THAT RULING'S OBJECTION, that ranking priority above status asserts a policy reflow2 must not default (dec:readiness-is-an-observation-the-threshold-is-the-judgement): the ranking is a RECOMMENDATION that a person overturns in one edit, and never a deletion on its own; a pair nothing separates gets no recommendation at all. The ladder is provenance, then live over withdrawn, then priority, then settled over open status, then connections; which is newer is shown and never weighed, and the node id is never a signal.

Built on reflow2 branch fix/the-engine-proposes-a-merge-and-a-person-picks-the-survivor. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
